text:
Tommy Novak was the 85th pick in 2015 and spent years proving he belonged. In Pittsburgh he's past that stage. He has 14 points in 19 games, 7 goals, and the Penguins carry the play with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 96th percentile of forwards last season for how much offense his team created with him out there, once linemates and opponents are accounted for.

Some of this year is running hot. He's shooting 20.6% against the 13.7% our numbers expect, and his on-ice goals are 5.2 ahead of the chances. His two-goal night against Los Angeles on November 7 helped end a four-game Penguins skid, but since then his minutes have dipped to about 13.

That's the thing to watch. On a team that has struggled to score, a center who drives play this well should be getting more ice, not less. The finishing will cool; the process is why Pittsburgh should keep leaning on him.
headline: Novak keeps outplaying his draft slot
